deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck determines the bounded operators T on a C*-algebra C that commute with right multiplications, T(xy)=T(x)y. In modern terms these are left centralizers, or left multipliers.

Argument for left multipliers: pass to the bidual. T'' is a weakly (σ(C'',C')) continuous endomorphism of the W*-algebra C'' (Sherman–Takeda). It commutes with x→xy for y∈C. By weak density of C in C'' and separate weak continuity of multiplication, it then commutes with x→xy for every y∈C''. Hence T''(y)=T''(1)y, so T is x→ux with u=T''(1)∈C''. Conversely, any u∈C'' with uC⊂C gives such a T. So the left multipliers form the normed algebra Γ_g={u∈C'': uC⊂C}.

Hermitian and positive multipliers: T is hermitian (resp. positive) iff x*T(x) is hermitian (resp. ≥0) for all x∈C. A hermitian u in Γ_g also satisfies Cu=(uC)*⊂C. This motivates the two-sided idealizer Γ={u∈C'': uC⊂C, Cu⊂C}, a C*-subalgebra of C''. In modern terms Γ is the multiplier algebra M(C) realized inside the enveloping von Neumann algebra.

Universal property: let C⊂R (R a C*-algebra) and Γ_1={x∈R: xC⊂C, Cx⊂C} be the idealizer of C in R. Each a∈Γ_1 defines the left multiplier x→ax of C, hence an element φ(a)∈C''. For hermitian a, φ(a) is hermitian and so lies in Γ; writing a=h+ik gives φ(Γ_1)⊂Γ. φ is a *-representation.

Next page: φ(a)=weak-lim ax along an approximate unit. If R is a von Neumann algebra with C weakly dense, the normal extension ψ:C''→R maps Γ into Γ_1, and φψ=id on Γ. This identifies M(C) with the idealizer of C in its weak closure (cf. Pedersen's book). The whole thing is the theory of the multiplier (double-centralizer) algebra of a C*-algebra, done via the bidual, in 1953.
errors: T is assumed continuous; automatic boundedness of centralizers is not addressed (it holds, by closed graph, but is not stated).
Γ_g is a closed subalgebra but not *-invariant. Only Γ is a C*-subalgebra; the page handles this correctly by passing to Γ.
The step 'φ(a) hermitian hence in Γ, hence φ(Γ_1)⊂Γ' tacitly uses that Γ_1 is *-closed, so a=h+ik with h,k hermitian in Γ_1. This is fine but unstated.
The injectivity statement on the next page (an element of Γ killed by R_* is 0) needs the representation C→R to be faithful. This is implicit in 'C⊂R'.

ideas.what: Left centralizers T(xy)=T(x)y of a C*-algebra are left multiplications by u∈C'' with uC⊂C, proved via the weakly continuous bitranspose
ideas.usually_credited_to: Wendel 1952 (L^1(G)); Johnson 1964 (centralizers of Banach algebras); Akemann–Pedersen–Tomiyama 1973 (C*-case via bidual)
ideas.where_published: Not in his 1957 'Un résultat sur le dual d'une C*-algèbre' as far as known

ideas.what: Two-sided idealizer of C in its bidual as the algebra of (double) multipliers, a C*-algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Busby 1968; Akemann–Pedersen–Tomiyama 1973 for the bidual idealizer description

ideas.what: For C⊂R, the idealizer Γ_1 of C in R maps *-homomorphically into Γ. When R is a von Neumann algebra with C weakly dense, Γ is identified with the idealizer of C in R.
ideas.modern_name: universal property of M(A); M(A) ≅ idealizer of A in A'' or in π(A)'' for faithful nondegenerate π
ideas.usually_credited_to: Busby 1968; Pedersen, C*-algebras and their automorphism groups 1979

missed.claim: A complete 1953 construction of the multiplier algebra of a C*-algebra. It is defined as the idealizer {u∈C'': uC⊂C, Cu⊂C} in the bidual, with a characterization of left centralizers and the universal map from idealizers in ambient algebras. This predates Busby (1968) and Akemann–Pedersen–Tomiyama (1973).
missed.quote: Soit Γ l'ensemble des u ∈ C'' tels que uC ⊂ C, Cu ⊂ C. C'est une sous-C*-algèbre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: the bidual-idealizer description of M(A), central in noncommutative topology, Kasparov KK-theory and crossed products, was apparently known to Grothendieck 15–20 years before its usual attribution.

deep.surprise_reason: Not new mathematics today. But a clean, essentially complete treatment of C*-multiplier algebras via the bidual in 1953 is an early unpublished appearance a specialist would find notable, and it is not credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The multiplications concerned are on the right (x→xy), so 'translations gauches' should be read with caution: the operators commute with right multiplications (left centralizers).
The garbled line after 'sous-C*-algèbre involutive' likely says that the hermitian elements of Γ_g lie in Γ ('les T hermitiens ... de Γ_g sont dans Γ').
'{+on aura+} ... etc faiblement (continues)' likely refers to multiplication being separately weakly continuous in C''.
